claim_verdicts.evidence: Flutter 3.47.2 run (git archive stage-1, probe test): bare Row(Text A, Text B) in a Scaffold -> two nodes, label "A" and "B". Same Row inside InkWell > ConstrainedBox > Padding (ProductTile without Semantics) -> ONE node, label "Chuột không dây\n450000 đ". flutter_test finders.dart (3.47.2): "The framework may combine semantics labels in certain scenarios, such as when multiple [Text] widgets are in a [TextButton]". Texts are not always separate nodes.
claim_verdicts.source: execution: flutter test (Flutter 3.47.2) on stage-1 copy; packages/flutter_test/lib/src/finders.dart bySemanticsLabel doc
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: A screen reader reads the description Flutter builds alongside the widget tree; each text widget adds its words to it. Depending on the widgets around them, two texts side by side may be read as two separate pieces or run together with no sign of what they mean. Wrapping them in a Semantics widget with one label, and excluding the pieces inside it, gives the reader one sentence you chose.

claim_verdicts.evidence: Flutter 3.47.2 widgets/basic.dart, Semantics.excludeSemantics: "Whether to replace all child semantics with this node. Defaults to false. When this flag is set to true, all child semantics nodes are ignored." Execution: ProductTile node label is exactly "Chuột không dây, 450000 đồng" (no Text labels appended).

Flutter 3.47.2 material/constants.dart: "The minimum dimension of any interactive region according to Material guidelines... a square of size kMinInteractiveDimension x kMinInteractiveDimension is the smallest acceptable region that should respond to gestures." kMinInteractiveDimension = 48.0. docs.flutter.dev accessibility checklist: "All tappable targets should be at least 48x48 pixels." android-devs: logical pixels "are basically the same as device-independent pixels".

git show stage-1 (75bf7d2): product_tile.dart:16-35 matches claim exactly (Semantics label '${product.name}, ${product.priceVnd} đồng', button: onTap != null, excludeSemantics: true, InkWell > ConstrainedBox(minHeight: 48) > Padding(all 12) > Row). product_catalog.dart:23 and :33 build ProductTile(product: products[index]) with no onTap. Semantics dump shows no isButton flag.

product_catalog_test.dart:38-44 at stage-1 matches the claim. flutter test on a git-archive copy of stage-1 DonHang.App (Flutter 3.47.2): 'each tile is at least 48 pixels tall and has a spoken label' passed; run ended "All tests passed!".
claim_verdicts.source: execution: flutter test in temp copy of examples/don-hang@stage-1 DonHang.App

claim_verdicts.evidence: minHeight is a floor, but whether the tile grows depends on the parent. Execution with a long wrapping name: list (width 360) tile height 124.0; grid (width 600) tile height 72.0 — GridView uses mainAxisExtent: 72 (product_catalog.dart:30), a fixed cell height, so the tile does not grow there. Short name: list 48.0, grid 72.0.
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: 3 — yes, the tile is still at least 48 tall; minHeight sets only a floor. In the one-column list a tile with two lines of text grows taller; in the grid every cell is a fixed 72 high, so it stays 72.

claim_verdicts.evidence: Second half supported: docs.flutter.dev ui-design-and-styling: "Controls that are too small are hard for many people to interact with and select." First half ("much cheaper to get right in a small widget ... than to fix across many screens later") is a cost comparison with no source, stated as fact in section 4.
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: It is not a separate feature added at the end. It is part of how each widget is built: when a small widget like a tile gets it right, every screen that reuses the tile gets it right too.

issues.text: Overstates that each text is its own piece. Execution (Flutter 3.47.2): the same Name/Price Row inside ProductTile's InkWell > ConstrainedBox, without the Semantics wrapper, yields ONE node "Chuột không dây\n450000 đ"; only a bare Row gives two nodes. Section 2 ('may announce ... separately') leans on the same idea.
issues.quote: each text widget adds its own piece to that description. Two texts side by side can be announced as two separate pieces.
issues.fix: Replace with claim 1 suggested_text (texts may be read as separate pieces or run together, depending on the widgets around them; the Semantics label gives one sentence you chose). In section 2 keep 'may' and add 'or run together as "Bàn phím cơ 1250000 đ" with nothing saying what the number is'.

issues.text: Unlisted claim, contradicted by execution: with excludeSemantics removed, ProductTile's texts are appended into the SAME node as the label — dump label becomes "Chuột không dây, 450000 đồng\nChuột không dây\n450000 đ" — not exposed as separate pieces.
issues.quote: the texts inside could also be exposed as their own separate pieces, so the reader may announce them in addition to the label
issues.fix: Replace answer 2 with: '2 — the two texts would be added to the same announcement after the label, so the reader says the name and price twice: "Chuột không dây, 450000 đồng, Chuột không dây, 450000 đ".' Add it to claims (kind behavior, flutter).

issues.text: Answer 3 is true only for the list. ProductCatalog's grid uses mainAxisExtent: 72, so a tile in the grid is always 72 high and does not grow; measured: long name list 124.0, grid 72.0.
issues.quote: `minHeight` sets only a floor, so a taller tile with two lines of text is allowed and simply grows.
issues.fix: Use claim 6 suggested_text for answer 3 (grows in the list; fixed 72 in the grid).

issues.text: Unlisted claim: exact-match behaviour of find.bySemanticsLabel is not in the ledger (claim 5 only says the test finds the label). It is true (finders.dart: 'either by [RegExp.hasMatch] or string equality'), but must be listed.
issues.quote: `find.bySemanticsLabel` looks for a widget whose semantic label is exactly the sentence a screen reader would announce
issues.fix: Add a claim: 'find.bySemanticsLabel with a String matches by string equality (a RegExp by hasMatch)', kind syntax, version_key flutter, source flutter_test finders.dart. No text change needed.

issues.text: Key 'a' is correct, but the explanation for 'b' is contradicted by execution: removing excludeSemantics does not produce 'Tai nghe' then '890000 đ' separately; it appends the texts to the label in one node. The reason given for rejecting b is false.
issues.quote: That is what excludeSemantics: true prevents.
issues.fix: Explanation b (en): 'The Semantics label replaces the two texts, so they are not read as their own pieces.' vi: 'Nhãn Semantics thay cho hai đoạn chữ, nên chúng không được đọc thành mảnh riêng.'

issues.text: Correct explanation repeats the overstated 'separate pieces' idea (see section 4 issue); key 'c' is right.
issues.quote: so two texts can come out as separate pieces unless a Semantics label joins them
issues.fix: en: 'A screen reader reads the description Flutter builds, not the screen; a Semantics label decides what one row says.' Mirror in vi.

issues.text: Explanation c says phones get the list, but ProductCatalog picks the list by LayoutBuilder width < 600, not by device type; a phone in landscape can be wider than 600. Option c is still wrong for the stated reason (mis-taps).
issues.quote: but phones get the one-column list
issues.fix: en c: 'The number of columns does not make a row shorter; the complaint is about hitting the wrong row.' Mirror in vi.
